sections.heading: C2 — Your Driver’s License
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Your Driver’s License

FACT_ID: sec01-R01 | anchor: A11
Changing information on a driver license can lead to severe penalties, including loss of the license. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-R02 | anchor: A11
Report a lost or destroyed license to the Bureau of Motor Vehicles and apply for a duplicate. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-R03 | anchor: A11
A renewal notice is mailed about 45 days before expiry to the latest address on the Bureau’s file. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-R04 | anchor: A11
Driving with an expired license is unlawful. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-R05 | anchor: A11
Notify the Bureau of Motor Vehicles within 30 days after your licensed name or address changes. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-R06 | anchor: A12
Driving contrary to a restriction on your license is unlawful. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R07 | anchor: A12
The Secretary of State may require a license examination or hearing even after a license has been issued. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R08 | anchor: A12
The Secretary of State may require a doctor’s statement about a driver’s physical or mental condition. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R09 | anchor: A12
A written adverse driving report from police or another member of the public can prompt the Secretary of State to suspend a license. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R10 | anchor: A12
A person who signed a minor’s license or instruction-permit application may later request suspension through a notarized written filing with the Secretary of State. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R11 | anchor: A12
Revocation ends the license and driving privilege and requires a new application when the revocation period ends. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R12 | anchor: A12
Vehicular manslaughter brings at least 5 years of revocation, and alcohol involvement makes that revocation permanent. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R13 | anchor: A12
Habitual-offender revocation lasts at least 1 year. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R14 | anchor: A12
After suspension, driving remains prohibited until the driver receives written reinstatement notice. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R15 | anchor: A12
Failure to file required insurance can result in suspension. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R16 | anchor: A12
Missing court for a traffic citation is a listed ground for license suspension. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R17 | anchor: A13
A conviction for eluding police, passing a roadblock or street racing may cause a suspension of up to 90 days. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R18 | anchor: A13
A conviction for driving after suspension may bring a further 60-day suspension. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R19 | anchor: A13
A conviction for failing to stop for a police officer may result in a 30-day license suspension. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R20 | anchor: A13
A conviction for leaving a crash scene involving bodily injury may result in a 30-day license suspension. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R21 | anchor: A13
A conviction for driving alone on a permit may result in a 30-day license suspension. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R22 | anchor: A13
A conviction for criminal operation without a license may result in a 30-day license suspension. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R23 | anchor: A13
A conviction for passing a stopped school bus displaying flashing red lights may result in a 30-day license suspension. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R24 | anchor: A13
A conviction for exceeding the posted speed limit by at least 30 miles per hour may result in a 30-day license suspension. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R25 | anchor: A13
A conviction for altering a license or registration certificate may result in a 30-day license suspension. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R26 | anchor: A13
A conviction for lending a license may result in a 30-day license suspension. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R27 | anchor: A13
A conviction for unlawful use of a license may result in a 30-day license suspension. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R28 | anchor: A13
A conviction for displaying a suspended license may result in a 30-day license suspension. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R29 | anchor: A13
A conviction for falsifying a registration or license application may result in a 30-day license suspension. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R30 | anchor: A13
A conviction for giving false information to a police officer may result in a 30-day license suspension. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R31 | anchor: A13
For an adjudicated first use of false credentials to obtain liquor or enter a drinking establishment by someone younger than 21, the court may suspend driving privileges for 30 days. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R32 | anchor: A13
For a second adjudicated false-identification liquor offense by someone younger than 21, the license suspension is 90 days. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R33 | anchor: A13
An adjudicated false-identification liquor offense after the second offense by someone younger than 21 brings a 1-year suspension. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R34 | anchor: A13
The false-identification liquor offense described for people younger than 21 carries 6 demerit points. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R35 | anchor: A14
Demerit points disappear from a driver’s record when they reach 1 year of age. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R36 | anchor: A14
A suspended driver is entitled to a Secretary of State hearing whose examiner can continue, change or reverse the action. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R37 | anchor: A14
At a suspension hearing the driver may have an attorney, and the hearing decision can be appealed to Superior Court. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R38 | anchor: A14
Recklessly speeding away after a police request or signal to stop, producing a chase with a police vehicle using a blue light and siren, is a Class C crime. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R39 | anchor: A14
If an attempt to elude police causes serious bodily injury to anyone, the driver commits a Class B crime. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R40 | anchor: A14
Knowingly, intentionally or recklessly failing to stop at a crash scene becomes a Class C crime when the crash causes serious bodily injury or death. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R41 | anchor: A14
Each calendar year without convictions or suspensions earns 1 violation-free credit point, up to a maximum of 4. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R42 | anchor: A14
The approved Maine Driving Dynamics course is a 5-hour driver-improvement program. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R43 | anchor: A14
Completing Maine Driving Dynamics or another approved improvement course deducts 3 points, with a deduction allowed only once in any 12-month period. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R44 | anchor: A15
Three license suspensions within 3 years may lead to an additional suspension lasting up to 120 days. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R45 | anchor: A15
Failing to appear on a motor-vehicle summons or to pay its related fine brings suspension until the appearance occurs or the fine is paid. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R46 | anchor: A15
Operating under the influence, an alcohol blood level of 0.08% or higher, or refusing a blood-alcohol test requires a mandatory suspension of a varying term. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R47 | anchor: A15
Driving to endanger requires a suspension of at least 30 days. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R48 | anchor: A15
Illegal liquor transport, possession or consumption by a minor in a motor vehicle requires at least 30 days of suspension. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R49 | anchor: A15
A minor’s illegal drug transportation in a motor vehicle requires a suspension of at least 30 days. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R50 | anchor: A15
If an uninsured driver is responsible for crash damage, the license and registration remain suspended until proof of insurance is filed with the Secretary of State. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R51 | anchor: A15
After reviewing the available evidence, the Secretary of State may suspend without a hearing a driver found incompetent because of physical or mental impairments. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R52 | anchor: A16
A suspended person may request a hearing, but the suspension can remain effective while the hearing is pending. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R53 | anchor: A16
A judge may suspend a license for contempt arising from an unpaid fine in a criminal or civil-violation proceeding. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R54 | anchor: A16
A judge may order a license suspension for an offense unrelated to driving. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R55 | anchor: A09
For the initial passenger restriction, immediate family includes grandparents, stepgrandparents, parents, stepparents, siblings, stepsiblings, children, stepchildren and a spouse, plus analogous foster-family members and, while living with that family, exchange students, court-appointed wards and a deployed military parent’s child under the family’s guardianship. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-R56 | anchor: A09
The required driving time must be certified on the Secretary of State’s form by a parent, stepparent, guardian or spouse. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-R57 | anchor: A09
When the applicant has no parent, a stepparent, guardian, spouse or employer may certify the driving time. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-R58 | anchor: A10
Changing a license classification requires all examinations applicable to that change. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-R59 | anchor: A10
A minor younger than 18 needs an application signature from a parent, a legal guardian with custody, or a spouse aged at least 18 for a license or instruction permit. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-R60 | anchor: A14
A person with no driving record may still receive credit for completing an approved driver-improvement course. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> pdf-0014]
